incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an elaborate artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating Leal to defraud immigrants, offering services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 cash payments and detainee release services. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office after seeing these fraudulent videos online.

The scams have escalated dramatically in recent months, with Leal's anti-piracy company removing nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms: 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The fraudulent scheme typically directs viewers to contact a WhatsApp number where scammers send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the origin of the scams and is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article featuring Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler has surfaced as part of a rising scam trend. The fabricated story promoted Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform, through the false confrontation. However, the interview never actually occurred. This type of deception represents a growing problem identified by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, which found that artificial intelligence technology is making investment scams increasingly convincing and difficult to detect.

ASIC's latest research reveals that scammers are building elaborate webs of deception using deepfake images and videos of well-known Australians. Last year, the regulator removed 19,400 scams overall, up 182 percent, including 7,051 fake investment platforms. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, politician Pauline Hanson, businessman Dick Smith, and billionaire Gina Rinehart are among frequently impersonated figures. ASIC warns consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers independently and to avoid investing with companies unable to provide verifiable credentials, while Alan Kohler argues that platforms distributing this content should face heavy financial penalties.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco accuses Oura, the smart ring company valued at $11 billion, of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit alleges that Oura Ring devices, priced at $300 and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as claimed in marketing materials. According to the lawsuit, the rings' algorithms and sensors lack the ability to detect necessary physiological signals and instead rely on unreliable artificial intelligence estimates compared to guessing. The complaint specifically challenges Oura's marketing claim of 95 percent sleep staging accuracy, noting that actual clinical sleep labs require complex equipment including multiple electrodes to measure brain activity.

Oura responded by defending its science and research, stating that its devices use multiple physiological signals including heart rate, heart rate variability, movement, breathing patterns, and temperature. The company maintains that its sleep staging has been validated against polysomnography, the medical standard for sleep studies, though it acknowledges the ring is not a medical device. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear at this stage what compensation affected customers might receive or whether they could participate in the suit. This marks another legal challenge for Oura, which is also facing an ongoing lawsuit over alleged unauthorized collection of personal data.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments and is using Cursor Agent artificial intelligence to conduct exploitation activities. The group operated a data leak site and targeted organizations across multiple countries. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to assist with hands-on attacks against ten target organizations. The Linux ransomware variant uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi-specific mode that kills running virtual machines to access their files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands.

The Aurora operators employed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan victim networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by searching internal subnets and checking ports 443 and 902. When using Cursor Agent, attackers provided credentials or network access and tasked the AI with standard exploitation activities like installing VPN clients, scanning networks, and attempting authentication relay attacks. A second Aurora cluster was identified conducting similar attacks using different techniques, including SQL Server exploitation and exfiltration to self-hosted storage. Gambit Security provided indicators of compromise including IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes associated with both clusters.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas claiming that the chain's artificial intelligence delivery management system caused over $100 million in damages to its business. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges that the mandatory Dragontail system created operational problems and customer dissatisfaction after its 2024 rollout. The franchisee says DoorDash drivers gained visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering immediately, which significantly delayed food arrival and reduced sales.

Before the system's implementation, Chaac maintained over 90% of deliveries within 30 minutes and posted double-digit sales growth. After Dragontail launched, delivery performance deteriorated sharply, with year-over-year sales in New York City dropping from positive 10.19% growth to negative 9.78%. The lawsuit claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training and support while ignoring the worsening delivery metrics. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the claims and will respond through legal channels. The case comes as Pizza Hut's parent company Yum Brands explores strategic options for the struggling brand.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other NPR personalities to defraud people by offering fake interview opportunities on the show "Fresh Air." Recipients receive highly personalized emails that reference their work and professional accomplishments, making the offers seem legitimate. The scheme escalates when victims are asked to pay fees for production costs. A Misericordia University history professor was among those targeted and became suspicious when asked for $250, noting that the initial contact came directly from Gross rather than through typical production assistants.

WHYY, NPR and law enforcement are investigating the fraudulent emails. Cybersecurity experts attribute the scam's effectiveness to artificial intelligence, which allows criminals to create convincing, personalized impersonations at minimal cost, replacing old tactics of mass emails with obvious errors. The emails often contain red flags such as unprofessional email addresses and requests for payment, which legitimate media organizations never require. WHYY has clarified that it never charges guests to appear and advised people to verify interview requests through official channels rather than responding to suspicious messages.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fraudulent think tank called the Hanover Institute, funded by the Israeli government, published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days to manipulate artificial intelligence systems into generating pro-Israel arguments. The non-existent institute, which has no legal entity, physical address, or named staff, presented its material as neutral research on contentious topics including allegations of genocide, war crimes, and prisoner torture. The site was designed using technology platforms optimized to make chatbots cite its content, and it was registered with the U.S. Justice Department as foreign agent material distributed for Israel.

The operation is part of a larger campaign funded by tens of millions in Israeli government money routed through intermediaries like European advertising firm Havas Media. Israeli officials have expressed doubt about these public diplomacy efforts, with some saying the government wasted substantial funds on the initiative. American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with polling showing only 36 percent of Americans sympathizing with Israel as of February, down from higher levels in previous years.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno. The labels accuse both companies of scraping thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their AI models and of directly reproducing sections of famous songs in their generated music. The record labels claim the companies have been deliberately evasive about what music they copied and that this constitutes willful copyright infringement on a massive scale. One lawsuit was filed in New York against Udio, while another was filed in Massachusetts against Suno.

To support their claims, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly recreate versions of famous copyrighted songs using specific prompts in both AI generators. They submitted a comprehensive list of thousands of copyrighted works they claim were scraped, including catalogs from artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, Michael Jackson, and many others. The labels created AI-generated examples showing the services producing music that closely mimics original songs, such as near-identical copies of Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" and Green Day's "American Idiot." The lawsuits represent a major legal battle over how generative AI services should handle copyrighted material.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized for using artificial intelligence to prepare legal filings in a Los Angeles lawsuit that contained fabricated case citations, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings. The case involves Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, who sued State Farm after a 2020 fire in her Carson home left it uninhabitable. When contractors attempted repairs, a storm caused additional water damage, and after delays in obtaining State Farm's approval, the work was never completed. Meni-Siliga and her husband exhausted their savings and retirement accounts, declared bankruptcy, and lost their home to foreclosure. State Farm claimed negligence by the plaintiff and contractor caused her damages. The trial is scheduled for October.

Attorney Jacquelene Robinson admitted that seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and misquoted passages. She used an AI tool called Irys, believing it was connected to her law firm's legal research subscription and would verify citations. Lead counsel Kenneth Katel apologized and accepted responsibility, stating the firm has updated its AI use policies. State Farm said it expects its external lawyers to meet the highest ethical standards and confirm accuracy of all filings.

stories.Headline: China promotes coordinated development of data industry, artificial intelligence-- Beijing Review
stories.Summary:
# Summary

China's data industry reached 6.78 trillion yuan in 2025, and the country is now focusing on coordinating development between its data sector and artificial intelligence capabilities. The 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo, held in Guiyang from August 28-30, attracted 372 companies and over 16,000 guests to showcase innovations in computing power, large models, and data circulation. Government officials emphasized that high-quality datasets are essential for advancing AI capabilities and that data technology is transforming traditional industries like power generation and renewable energy forecasting.

Beyond upgrading existing industries, data and AI are creating new business opportunities and employment categories. Companies are hiring data collectors to train robots through embodied intelligence projects, while micro-enterprises and one-person startups are emerging as signs of entrepreneurial growth. International participants from Zimbabwe, Chile, Pakistan, and other nations attended to explore cooperation opportunities, with officials highlighting the potential for shared benefits and technological exchange between countries through collaborative data and AI development.

stories.Headline: Who Writes AI's Rules When Someone Else Owns the Machines?
stories.Summary:
# Summary

South Africa withdrew its Draft National AI Policy in April 2026 after discovering that at least six of its 67 academic references were fabricated, highlighting a broader challenge facing the Global South. The incident underscores a critical debate about who controls artificial intelligence governance and infrastructure. Currently, the United States and China host roughly 86% of global data centre capacity, giving them power to set rules and prices for AI systems worldwide. This concentration of computing power represents what critics call "tech colonialism," where developing nations provide data and demand but lack ownership and control over the technology itself.

BRICS countries and other Global South nations are attempting to shift AI governance away from Western-led standards by emphasizing digital sovereignty and development rights. They are seeking to anchor AI governance within the United Nations rather than OECD-led bodies and have established organizations like the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation. However, meaningful sovereignty requires owning physical infrastructure, not just adopting policies. The article notes that until developing nations build regional computing capacity and chip manufacturing capabilities, they remain dependent on foreign platforms controlled by American hyperscalers or Chinese firms. True sovereignty means choosing dependencies rather than having them imposed.

Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

stories.Headline: EU places ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox under strictest platform rules
stories.Summary:
The European Union has classified ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under its Digital Services Act. These three American companies will now face direct supervision from the European Commission and must comply with stricter requirements designed to address risks related to children, election integrity, and public security. The rules apply to services with over 45 million users in the EU, bringing the total number of regulated platforms to 28.

Companies failing to meet the new requirements within four months face fines up to 6 percent of their annual global revenue. Reddit reported 57.2 million EU users in July, while Roblox has 46.6 million. OpenAI stated it would prepare to meet ChatGPT's additional obligations, and Roblox welcomed the designation, emphasizing safety's importance. This designation adds another regulatory layer for ChatGPT, which already complies with the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

The financial services company is expanding its engineering team despite increased AI involvement, demonstrating its commitment to using productivity gains for expansion rather than workforce reduction. AI-assisted development is integrated throughout the engineering lifecycle, including code writing, testing, debugging and documentation. The company plans to continue deepening AI adoption across both engineering and consumer-facing experiences to expand innovation, improve productivity and deliver more personalized financial services at scale.

stories.Headline: Not Nvidia. Not AMD. This Semiconductor Giant Will Be the Ultimate Winner of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Hardware Race.
stories.Summary:
# Summary

The article argues that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, not Nvidia or AMD, will be the ultimate winner in the artificial intelligence hardware race. While many investors focus on chip designers like Nvidia and AMD, the author contends that Taiwan Semiconductor holds the real advantage because it manufactures chips for these companies and controls approximately 72 percent of the global foundry market. Since Nvidia and AMD do not build their own chips, they must rely on Taiwan Semiconductor's manufacturing capacity.

Taiwan Semiconductor benefits from a neutral position in the competition between chip designers, meaning it will profit regardless of which company's hardware becomes dominant. The company's CEO expects elevated demand for chips to continue through at least 2029 or 2030, providing several more years of strong growth. Additionally, Taiwan Semiconductor plans to launch new chip technology that will allow for price increases, positioning it as one of the safest investments in the artificial intelligence sector.

To support this strategy, OptiValue has formed partnerships with Eagle Infrastructure India for intelligent infrastructure development and with SFJ Business Solutions for AI transformation programmes. Chairman Ashish Kumar emphasized the company's goal to connect artificial intelligence with physical systems across defence and critical infrastructure, positioning digital twins as a bridge between digital engineering and operational intelligence for improved organizational resilience.

stories.Headline: The S&P 500 Has Fallen in 56% of Septembers Since 1928. Here's What That Means for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks.
stories.Summary:
Historical data shows that the S&P 500 has fallen in 56% of Septembers since 1928, with an average decline of about 1.17% during that month. This pattern, known as the September Effect, may stem from psychological expectations, investor profit-taking, tax-loss harvesting strategies, and major Federal Reserve decisions that typically occur in September. However, the market has risen in 44% of Septembers, and the average declines are relatively modest.

Despite potential September volatility affecting the broader market, artificial intelligence stocks like Nvidia and Micron Technology remain strong investments. Nvidia recently reported revenues that more than doubled year-over-year to $96.2 billion, with management forecasting 70% revenue growth ahead. Micron is also performing strongly and reports earnings in late September. Both companies are leaders in the AI infrastructure sector, with tech companies expected to spend $1.3 trillion on data center buildouts next year, suggesting that any September price declines in these stocks could present buying opportunities for investors.
